issues: Pre-existing (NOT a refactor regression): the react-hot-toast 'Vérifiez votre email' fixed-bottom banner sits ON TOP of the cancel-ride-btn (Annuler la course) inside the bottom sheet and intercepts pointer events. Playwright force=True click was still swallowed; only a JS .click() bypass worked. Real users on unverified accounts may experience trouble tapping 'Annuler la course' until the toast is dismissed. Recommendation: either render the verify-email toast above the bottom sheet (z-index lower than ride bottom sheet), or auto-hide it on /ride/* routes.

context_for_next_testing_agent: RideTrackingPage refactor (TrackingBanners.jsx extraction) is CERTIFIED no-regression. The 'assigned/en route/in_progress' driver states are dispatch-dependent in preview and were not exercised, but the rendering paths for those states (lines 879-1086 in RideTrackingPage.js) use the same StatusDialog/PoolBadge/FlightWatchBanner/RentalMeterBanner imports that were verified working in the searching state — so they are wired correctly. Known UX caveat: the 'Vérifiez votre email' toast at the bottom of the screen intercepts the 'Annuler la course' button click for unverified accounts; use page.evaluate('document.querySelector(...).click()') to bypass it in scripts, OR dismiss the toast first by clicking its X. Test flow that worked: login -> /course -> type 'Schoelcher Martinique' in 'Où allez-vous ?' -> wait 2.5s -> click .pac-item -> wait 4.5s -> click ride-choose-request-btn -> on /ride/{id}, dismiss cancel-policy-ok if shown -> JS-click cancel-ride-btn -> click any cancel-reason-* -> verify ride-cancelled-banner appears.
rca of the issue: No bug found in the refactor. The one test-script wrinkle (cancel-modal didn't open on first click with playwright force=True) was traced to the pre-existing 'Vérifiez votre email' react-hot-toast overlay covering the cancel button — NOT a regression introduced by the extraction. Solved in-script by using a JS .click() bypass and verified the full searching -> cancel -> cancelled flow works end-to-end with 0 console errors and all extracted-component data-testids rendering correctly.
